_comment: CALABI_COORD_DERP_MAP_FILE — the relay directory calabi-coord distributes to mesh
nodes (MESH.4 B2b). Use this INSTEAD of CALABI_COORD_DERP_ADDR once the
deployment runs more than one calabi-derp.
Each host_name:derp_port MUST be the public address mesh clients can dial:
a node listens on the relay its home region resolves to here, and peers send
to it through exactly that address. A region listed with an address clients
cannot reach makes every node that homes there unreachable by relay.
stun_port must match that relay's relay.stun_port: clients measure their
latency to each region over STUN to choose a home, and a region with no
stun_port cannot be measured, so it is never chosen.
home_region is only the default stamped on a node before it has measured
anything — clients replace it with their own measurement.
Mount it read-only and point calabi-coord at it:
volumes:
- ./mesh/derp-map.json:/etc/calabi/derp-map.json:ro
environment:
CALABI_COORD_DERP_MAP_FILE: /etc/calabi/derp-map.json
usage_collection (F2) maps a region code to the base URL calabi-coord drains
that relay's byte counters from. It is a SEPARATE section on purpose:
'regions' above is broadcast to every mesh node, while this address is
internal and is reached with a credential. Never merge the two.
The relay must be started with a relay usage token, and calabi-coord with the
same value in CALABI_COORD_RELAY_USAGE_TOKEN. Omit a region here and that relay
is simply not collected — which is exactly what a user's self-hosted relay
does: its traffic never reaches the platform's accounting at all.
Prefer https. The token and the traffic graph both cross this link.
